clue.text: Island nation adopting incredibly wise candidate for high office

indicators.note: a country that adopts something takes it into its own family, so one word goes inside the other
something done incredibly is done in an unbelievable way, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: a nation is a land
the letters of wise, rearranged
Kamala Harris, US presidential candidate in 2024

explanation.surface: A country takes in an improbably clever presidential hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris is the largest island of the Outer Hebrides off Scotland; the 'candidate' is Kamala Harris, who ran for US president in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis and Harris is a single landmass in Scotland's Western Isles, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Provider, wasting energy once, recycles paper the wrong way

indicators.note: wasting means losing, and once limits the loss of the energy symbol to a single occurrence
going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the whole string is read from its end

blocks.note: to recycle something is to reuse it
E is the symbol for energy
the i is a British national newspaper, sister title of the Independent

explanation.surface: A supplier cuts its energy use, then recycles paper badly.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is dropped from REUSES, giving REUSS; add I and read REUSSI backwards to get ISSUER.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer is one who supplies or hands out something, such as tickets or shares, so is a provider.

clue.text: Like a lazy, indolent slacker, say, given no slack over branch of philosophy

definitions.text: Like a lazy, indolent slacker, say

blocks.note: a rope with no slack is taut
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
logic is a branch of philosophy

explanation.surface: Describes an idle loafer who is suddenly forced to tighten up over some philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: 'lazy, indolent slacker' says the same thing three times, which is what tautology means.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautologic means needlessly repetitive, and lazy, indolent and slacker all repeat the same idea.

clue.text: Hack probing new line-up of hot rock group

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one word is placed within another
a new line-up puts the same members in a different order

blocks.note: to hack is to hew
the letters of hot, reordered

explanation.surface: A journalist digs into a band's latest line-up of hot talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, but here it is the verb meaning chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who are a famous English rock band from the 1960s, so the name is an example of a rock group.

clue.text: Hail Roman supporting Republican Party

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting part sits underneath, so it is written second

blocks.note: R is short for Republican
ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail

explanation.surface: A Roman salutes the Republican Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican Party' reads as one phrase, but Party alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively party with dance music, so the noun means a party.

clue.text: Flying metal planes flying around without personnel

indicators.note: letters flying around are tossed about and land in a new order
without in its old sense of outside means the letters surround something

blocks.note: the letters of planes, rearranged
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Pilotless aircraft circle overhead while shrapnel flies.
explanation.walkthrough: HR sits inside a rearrangement of planes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is the fragments of metal thrown out by an exploding shell, so it is metal sent flying.

clue.text: Wrap we hasten to cook

indicators.note: to cook is to work raw ingredients into a different form, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to hurry up and get the wrap cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' looks like a tortilla meal; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enswathe is to bind or envelop in cloth, so it is a verb meaning wrap.

clue.text: Ways to package doughnut affecting quality

indicators.note: to package something is to wrap it up, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: paths are ways
a ring doughnut is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Methods of wrapping doughnuts that change their quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affecting' looks like a verb meaning changing; here it means moving the emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or speech that arouses pity or sadness, so it is a quality that affects people.

clue.text: Discern extremely rare jackets using a single pin in retail area

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters only
a jacket covers whatever is worn underneath, so these letters go around another piece

blocks.note: to scent something is to detect or discern it
the outside letters of rare
pins are legs, and moving on one leg is hopping

explanation.surface: Spotting unusual jackets fastened with one pin in a shopping area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' is slang for leg, so 'using a single pin' is HOPPING; it goes inside SCENTRE after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping centre is a complex of shops, which is a retail area.

clue.text: Spanish in Libya's capital swan around outside together

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping around something, so one piece surrounds another
turning around means facing the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Libya'

blocks.note: en is Spanish for in
a cob is a male swan
the first letter of Libya

explanation.surface: Spaniards in Tripoli see a swan swimming about outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Libya's capital' suggests Tripoli, but it is just its first letter; the swan surrounds it before the pair is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is a French phrase meaning all together as one unit, so it is an adverb for together.

clue.text: Current time to retire for Macron or possible White House resident?

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
nuit is French for night, the time to go to bed for the French president

explanation.surface: Asks whether bedtime has come for France's president, or for whoever lives in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' suggests the US president, but here it is an igloo, a house made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit people of the Arctic traditionally built igloos, white houses of snow, so one could live in one.

clue.text: Wanting run, Victor Borge's heading past camper

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the word
a heading is at the top, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: a victor is a winner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the first letter of Borge
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Victor Borge, the comic pianist, appears to be heading past a camper van without running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor Borge' reads as the entertainer's name, but Victor is the winner and Borge only gives B. One R is dropped from WINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winnebago is a large American brand of motorhome, so it is a camper in the vehicle sense.

clue.text: Either a lark or a gull in springtime?

blocks.note: first meaning: a prank, a piece of fun
second meaning: someone duped on the first day of the fourth month

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about seeing a lark or a gull, two birds, in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Lark and gull look like birds, but a lark is a jape and a gull is a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the trick played on 1 April and the person tricked, so it is a jape or a dupe.

clue.text: Team given one of Pep's tips - be brave!

indicators.note: a word has two tips, its ends, and this asks for one of them

blocks.note: Man U is the nickname of Manchester United football club
Pep begins and ends with P

explanation.surface: A football side gets advice from Pep Guardiola, Manchester City's manager: be brave!
explanation.walkthrough: Pep Guardiola manages Manchester City, United's rivals, which makes the surface wry.
explanation.definitionFit: To man up is an idiom for summoning courage, so it is an order to be brave.

clue.text: One remarkably aged wine in this

blocks.note: first meaning: the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years
second meaning: a very large wine bottle, holding eight standard bottles

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a wine that has aged remarkably well.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a vintage wine; the two halves are separate meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis patriarch is the byword for great age, and the same name is used for a big champagne bottle.

clue.text: Act half-heartedly boxing fighter, old one like Achilles?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and half of it is taken away
boxing something puts it in a box, so the other pieces are enclosed

blocks.note: a deed is an act
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A half-hearted performance from a boxer in an ancient-style epic.
explanation.walkthrough: The act word has two letters at its heart and loses one of them; 'fighter' is a warplane, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was born of a sea-nymph and a mortal, so he was a demigod, half divine; the question mark marks him as an example.

clue.text: Means to be heard, entertaining earl with improbable irony, perhaps

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so the following letters go within

blocks.note: a mic, short for microphone, is a means of being heard
E is an abbreviation for earl
an improbable story is a tall one

explanation.surface: Describes a way of being heard by entertaining a nobleman with far-fetched irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irony' is read not as sarcasm but as 'like iron', an adjective; 'Means to be heard' looks like a homophone signal but is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irony in this literal sense has the qualities of iron, and iron is a metal, so the word is an example of metallic.

clue.text: Make low dive after emptying plane, banking roughly

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, so only the outer letters remain
banking means depositing something for safe keeping, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: dive without its inside letters
a jet is a plane
c, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a plane into a steep dive after unloading it, banking roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' looks like an aircraft tilting, but here JET takes C inside it. 'After' in the surface hints at order too.
explanation.definitionFit: To deject someone is to make them feel low in spirits, so it is a verb meaning depress.

clue.text: Group defending Alaba's header, with cheers from Barcelona maybe

indicators.note: a header sits at the top, so just the first letter is taken
a group defending something surrounds it, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: a clan is a group
the first letter of Alaba
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A football defence copes with a header from Real Madrid's David Alaba, to cheers from the Barcelona fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header' suggests football, but it means the first letter; 'cheers' is thanks, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the capital of Catalonia, so someone from there may well be Catalan, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: AA member, say, I installed in cooler room

indicators.note: something installed in a space is fitted inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: AC, air conditioning, is a cooler
a member of Alcoholics Anonymous is teetotal, TT
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker is put in the cooler, a prison room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AA' could be the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service; here it is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members are TT. 'Cooler' also suggests a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: Man in the street knocked back drink with melting ice, drinking litres behind bar

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but read here as sent back, so it runs the other way
melting ice loses its shape and reforms, so the letters change order
drinking takes something in, so the letters go inside
behind means coming after, so the litres follow the bar in sequence

blocks.note: OJ is orange juice
the letters of ice, rearranged
a pub is a bar
L is the symbol for litres

explanation.surface: An ordinary bloke at the bar downs a drink with the ice melting and orders litres more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads as downing a drink, but it signals reversal; the bar and litres go inside the melted ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Public is an idiom for the ordinary person, the same as the man in the street.

clue.text: East African runner maintaining small store on a farm

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: E is short for east
a runner can be a river, and the Nile runs through Africa
S is short for small

explanation.surface: An East African athlete keeps a small shop on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East African runner' suggests a Kenyan athlete; the runner is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensile is to preserve fodder as silage in a silo, which is how a farm stores crops.

clue.text: Would-be fancy car filled by Bobby

indicators.note: something filled by another thing has it inside, so the second piece goes within

blocks.note: a Lada is a Russian make of car
a bobby is a British police officer; DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer squeezes into a car that wants to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer, here a DI, detective inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone affectedly posh, pretending to refinement, so it means would-be fancy.

clue.text: What lovers do in luxury car is tops

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, the car holding the action

blocks.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce
lovers neck, kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Kissing in the back of a Rolls-Royce is the best thing there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' looks like the slang for excellent; it is garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Roll-necks are sweaters with high folded collars, so they are tops in the clothing sense.

clue.text: Oscar slicing bean for a fresh starter

indicators.note: slicing goes into the middle of something, so this letter sits inside

blocks.note: bean and nob are both slang for the head
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Cutting up a bean for a fresh appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bean' and 'starter' suggest cooking; bean is slang for the head and a starter is a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A noob is internet slang for a newcomer, someone freshly starting out.

clue.text: Ethan's coat put on back-to-front?

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the outside letters of Ethan
to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: Ethan has put his coat on the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-to-front' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition: things arranged end on meet back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: End on means with an end facing forwards, as when vehicles queue one behind another, the back of one at the front of the next.

clue.text: A song I composed? Miss this for musical entertainment

indicators.note: a composed song is put together from parts in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A songwriter suggests skipping their own tune for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb meaning skip; it is a title, completing the name of a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Saigon is a hit stage musical, so adding this city name to Miss gives a piece of musical entertainment.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper behind Obama, initially, or Bush

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only
behind means following, so this piece is written after the other

blocks.note: the first letter of Obama
in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero

explanation.surface: A fan of heroes lines up behind Obama, or Bush, two US presidents.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama and Bush suggest presidents; Bush is the definition, a plant, and the Hero is the mythical priestess loved by Leander.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub, so it is a kind of bush.
